name: J. A. VanEeghen
bio: J. A. VanEeghen ran a horse ranch on Garner creek, and in February 1885 the paper noted he came back from the East wearing a plug hat full of bullet holes. He joined the Little Missouri River Stockmen's Association in April 1885, first ran his horse brand in the Cow Boy in August 1885, and repeatedly advertised rewards for strayed horses. In March and April 1886 he sold his band of horses to B. F. Lamb, then went west and returned in July with two to three hundred head, mostly mares. In August 1886 he shipped a car of horses to St. Cloud, Minn., and in October he moved his post office to Sentinel Butte.
